chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Makfuf narrated to me; he said: Some of our companions narrated to me from some of the phlebotomists of al-ʿAskar who were Christians.

That Abu Muhammad عليه السلام sent for me one day at the time of Salat al-Zuhr and said to me, "Perform phlebotomy on this vein." He then showed me a vein that I did not recognize among the veins that are usually opened. So I said to myself, "I have never seen a matter stranger than this: he is ordering me to perform phlebotomy at the time of Zuhr, though it is not a time for phlebotomy, and secondly it is a vein I do not know."

Then he said to me, "Wait and remain in the house." When evening came, he called me and said, "Release the blood." So I released it. Then he said to me, "Stop," so I stopped. Then he said to me, "Remain in the house." When it was midnight, he sent for me and said to me, "Release the blood." He said: I was even more astonished than at my first astonishment, and I disliked to ask him. He said: So I released it, and white blood came out as though it were salt. He then said to me, "Restrain it," so I restrained it. Then he said, "Remain in the house."

When morning came, he ordered his steward to give me three dinars. I took them and went out until I came to Ibn Bakhtishuʿ the Christian, and I recounted the story to him. He said to me, "By Allah, I do not understand what you are saying, nor do I recognize it in any branch of medicine, nor have I read it in any book. And I do not know in our time anyone more knowledgeable about the books of the Christians than so-and-so the Persian, so go to him." He said: So I hired a boat to al-Basrah, went to al-Ahwaz, then proceeded to فارس to my companion and informed him of the report. He said, "Give me some days." So I gave him time. Then I came to him asking for the answer. He said to me, "This that you are relating from this man was done once by al-Masih in his time."

key_terms.افْصِدْ: perform phlebotomy; open a vein to let blood flow
key_terms.الْعِرْقَ: the vein indicated for the procedure
key_terms.الْمَسِيحُ: the Messiah, cited as having performed such an act once in his time
key_terms.دَمٌ أَبْيَضُ: white blood, described as an extraordinary occurrence
key_terms.سَرِّحِ الدَّمَ: release the blood; allow the blood to flow
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الظُّهْرِ: the noon salat, the time at which the Imam عليه السلام summoned the phlebotomist
key_terms.قَهْرَمَانَهُ: his steward or household agent entrusted with payment

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kafi relate about the extraordinary sign shown by Imam al-Hasan al-ʿAskari عليه السلام to a Christian phlebotomist?
ai.summary: This narration recounts an extraordinary medical act witnessed from Abu Muhammad عليه السلام by a Christian phlebotomist, who found it contrary to known medical practice and beyond his understanding. After consulting learned Christian physicians, the event was described as something previously done only by al-Masih, highlighting the exceptional status and knowledge of the Imam عليه السلام.
